set.descent_text: The last pitch ends on a wide, loose ledge near the top of the face, the same ledge that Stone Monkey and Three Stoners reach. Walk along the grassy ledge toward Chiefshead, then zigzag down to the talus on the safest line, which is visible from above and has only a couple of short third-class steps. A faster alternative is the east and southeast side (third to fourth class) back to the northeast side, or third-class slopes on the southwest side. A ramp that is hidden from above also leads down, but it is easy to get cliffed out there. Parties with double ropes can also rappel the route from the top anchor of All Two Obvious.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Age Axe takes the prow at the left end of the northeast face. Go to the left side of the face and round the prow onto the southeast side, where a slab apron with right-facing flakes on its right marks the start. About 100 feet above it is a large roof-capped corner, and the start is roughly 100 feet right of East Prow.

review.notes: MP route page: apron start, prow, ledge walk-offs; trail page and route pages agree on Black Lake at about 5 miles; trip page lists the three descent options.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit ledge at a bolted anchor. Parties usually rappel the line with two ropes, staying mostly left of the route, and about five rappels reach the base. Otherwise walk off: the east and southeast side (third to fourth class) drops back to the northeast side, or third-class slopes on the southwest side lead down.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts from Middle Earth Ledge, just below the left side of the Eye of Mordor, the large eye-shaped feature on the lower part of the wall. Several easier pitches reach the ledge; the first pitch of Sykes' Sickle is a direct way up.

review.notes: Route page: rap the route with two ropes or walk off, summit ledge, start below Eye of Mordor; two trip pages and the Spear Me page agree on five double-rope rappels and the walk-offs.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on a descent ledge near the top. Walk southwest (to the left when facing uphill) a long way across an open ledge and meadow, following a few cairns and a faint trail. At some point you must downclimb a little to reach the top of a long ramp that falls to the northeast; it is very easy to cliff out if you turn too early or too late, so take care to find the right place. That ramp is unpleasant in wet or icy conditions. A safer alternative is to continue farther along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus, or to descend third-class slopes on the southwest side.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. East Prow follows the south nose of Spearhead, a blunt arete that is slabby at its base. The start is the most prominent clean right-facing dihedral just left of the prow, about 100 feet left of where Age Axe begins.

review.notes: East Prow page: ledge walk-off, cliff-out warning, start location. Age Axe page: the safer ledge zigzag. Trip report: southwest and east-southeast options.

set.descent_text: From the summit, the standard way down is the third-class scree and slabs on the southwest side. Descend well to the southwest before contouring around, because angling over early puts you above cliffs, then contour back around to the base of the climb. The fourth-class ramp on the southeast side is the other option.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The North Ridge starts at the northwest corner of the mountain. Choose the line carefully: a pronounced groove above a slab, near the highest point of ground, is the correct start, and parties that wander off it end up on much harder terrain.

review.notes: Route page: approach, start, SW descent. Trip pages: third-class SW slopes or fourth-class SE ramp.

set.descent_text: The upper pitches finish near the top of the face, and from there you walk off as for the other routes on the wall: third-class slopes on the southwest side, or the fourth-class ramp on the east and southeast side. To bail from lower down, rap anchors sit on a large ledge well left of the line above the fourth pitch, and two ropes are needed to get off from there.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts at the left side of the wall, with a long easy first pitch to a double ledge system. The Eye of Mordor, the elliptical feature in the lower left of the wall, lies up and left of the early pitches and seeps even in dry years.

review.notes: Route page: start, ledge system, rap anchors above pitch four, two ropes to bail. Trip pages: walk-off options.

set.descent_text: The route finishes with the upper pitches of East Prow and Age Axe, so it ends on the same ledge near the top of the face. From there walk southwest along the open ledge toward the cairns and faint trail, then downclimb to the top of the long northeast-facing ramp; the turn is easy to miss and leads to cliffs if overshot. A safer alternative is to keep going along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus, or to take third-class slopes on the southwest side.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Prowess leaves the ground as East Prow does, then moves up and left into its own systems before merging with Age Axe at the 3-inch crack and corner above the third belay.

review.notes: Route page: starts as East Prow and rejoins above; East Prow and Age Axe pages: ledge walk-off.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit. There are three ways down: rappel the route to the base with double ropes from the anchor at the top of the final pitch of All Two Obvious (about five rappels), descend the east and southeast side at third to fourth class back to the northeast side, or scramble down third-class slopes on the southwest side. The east and southeast side is quickest if your gear is at the base of the route.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts from Middle Earth Ledge, to the right of the Eye of Mordor, a huge vertical gouge left of center on the east face. Several ways lead to the ledge; the first pitch of Sykes' Sickle is the most direct.

review.notes: Route page and trip pages agree on the three descents and five double-rope rappels, and on the start from Middle Earth Ledge.

set.descent_text: After the Stone Monkey pitch and the 5.8 crack above it, the line exits to the ledge near the top of the face. Walk off the east and southeast side at third to fourth class, or take third-class slopes on the southwest side, or rappel the route from the top anchor of All Two Obvious with double ropes. If you took the Age Axe finish, the usual ledge walk-off applies: along the grassy ledge toward Chiefshead and a zigzag down to the talus.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Stone Monkey is a single hard pitch high on the face. Reach it by climbing the first three pitches of Scimitar to a grassy ledge, or the early pitches of Three Stoners.

review.notes: Route page: crux pitch, exit; trip page: Scimitar and Three Stoners lead to its base, finish via Four Believers or Age Axe; descent options.

set.descent_text: The seventh pitch steps right around an overhang onto third-class ground below the summit, and a short scramble reaches the top. From the summit, descend third-class scree on the southwest side, or take the fourth-class ramp on the southeast side. Both are loose and disorienting; trend climber's left and do not be discouraged if the line looks like it may cliff out.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Sykes' Sickle starts in the middle of the face at two parallel cracks. The first pitch follows the wide, left-arcing crack at the center of the wall, easy to spot from below.

review.notes: Route page: start and top-out; Barb page and trip page: summit walk-offs.

set.descent_text: The route tops out on the Barb Flake, which meets the North Ridge. You can finish by downclimbing the back of the flake (about 5.10a) and climbing the last two pitches of the North Ridge to the summit, or rappel without topping out. From the summit, walk off third-class scree to the southwest or the fourth-class ramp to the southeast, both loose, with the correct line trending climber's left. The rappels follow the Kingfisher line and several are needed. A 70 m rope works except for the last, which is close to 40 m once the snow has melted, so bring an 80 m rope or a retrievable single-rope rappel device. Anchor quality varies, so check every one.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts up a left-facing flake low on the face and works up to Middle Earth Ledge, with the Kingfisher on the left edge of the flake above.

review.notes: Route page descent section and two trip pages agree on the flake top-out, summit walk-offs, the 40 m final rappel and the rope lengths.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the very tip of the Barb Flake. Rappel the line from the top of the seventh pitch; every belay has chains. A 70 m rope works for all rappels except the last, which is about 40 m after the snow melts, so use an 80 m rope or a retrievable single-rope rappel device. As an alternative, downclimb the back of the flake (tricky, about 5.10a) and finish on the last two pitches of the North Ridge, then walk off the summit by the southeast ramp (fourth class) or the southwest scree (third class).
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts about 50 feet right of the big crack that begins Sykes' Sickle, at a small right-facing corner with a seep to its right. Two bolts lead to the corner; they are buried under snow in early summer.

review.notes: Route page and trip page agree on the rappel line, 40 m final rappel and the flake downclimb option; route page gives start and bolts.

set.descent_text: The route finishes with the last two or three pitches of the North Ridge, so it ends at the summit. Descend third-class scree on the southwest side, or the fourth-class ramp on the southeast side. Head well southwest before contouring around, because the ground below can cliff out, then return to the base of the face.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The Ten Essentials begins on Sykes' Sickle in the middle of the face, up the two parallel cracks, and uses its first three pitches.

review.notes: Route page: first three pitches of Sykes Sickle then North Ridge; North Ridge page and trip page: descent.

set.descent_text: The final pitch finishes on either the East Prow or the Age Axe line, so you reach the ledge near the top of the face. Walk off along the open ledge southwest, find the top of the long northeast-facing ramp after a short downclimb (easy to cliff out if you miss it), or go farther along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus with a couple of short third-class sections. Third-class slopes on the southwest side are another option, or the east and southeast side at third to fourth class.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Three Stoners starts on the low-angle slabs at the far left shoulder of the face, traversing up and right to a finger crack where the first belay sits.

review.notes: Route page: start and finishes; East Prow and Age Axe pages and trip page: ledge walk-offs.

set.descent_text: After Longs Peak, leave the Keyhole Route and drop off cross-country down the talus slopes into Glacier Gorge; the Trough is one such line. Then follow the trail back out the way you came in. Water on the ridge is hard to find unless snow or runoff is present, so carry what you need.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The traverse starts by climbing Spearhead, with a choice of route from the North Ridge up to harder lines.

review.notes: Route page: approach, descent and water note; North Ridge page: approach to the base.
